A chitosan-rich film-forming matrix blended with PVA and loaded with 1D attapulgite carrying retained phosphoric acid.  This combines the supported chitosan-attapulgite confinement motif with a PVA film former and free phosphoric acid rather than the reported PWA-containing composite. The quaternary design directly targets cold-side continuity using an OH-rich host plus 1D confinement.  cold_window: plausible bound-acid continuity in an OH-rich flexible matrix  nanoconfinement: 1D clay can organize interconnected acid pathways  retention: chitosan plus attapulgite should suppress phosphoric-acid loss  A starch-PVA blend film incorporating halloysite nanotubes preloaded or contacted with phosphoric acid to create confined acid channels.  The instance merges a known starch/PVA hydrogen-bonded host with HNT-based acid confinement not reported together in the provided pool. It is novel because each element is supported separately, but the integrated cold-oriented architecture is only analogous.  cold_window: starch/PVA hydrogen-bond network may retain bound polar continuity  nanoconfinement: HNT lumen and surface can host acid and limit leaching  proton_transfer: phosphoric-acid-rich confined domains should support hybrid hopping/vehicular transport  A chitosan membrane plasticised with a choline-chloride/phosphoric-acid deep eutectic to provide a retained acid-like conducting phase. The novelty lies in translating the DES evidence toward a colder, phosphoric-acid-centered composition rather than a generic DES blend.  cold_window: DES motif is plausible for non-crystallising bound-fluid continuity near 200 K  flexibility: DES-plasticised chitosan should reduce glassy disconnects  retention: chitosan can hold high polar-phase uptake without disintegration  An amorphous phosphate glass with proton-substituted phosphate network functionality used as the primary proton-conducting phase.
